Definition: a (sudden) alarm (properly, the object feared, by implication, the feeling)
BiblicalUsage: Pachad is sudden terror, dread that falls on people. Jacob calls God the Fear of Isaac, fear and dread fall on the nations at the Red Sea, Job says the thing he greatly feared has come upon him, and the psalmist is told not to be afraid of the terror by night.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe there are two kinds of dread in this word. The terror falls on God's enemies, and the terror God's people are told not to fear, because the Fear of Isaac is on their side.
RelatedEvents: The Exodus and the Red Sea
